questions.knowledge_point: Determining Vertical Asymptotes of Rational Functions by Factoring the Numerator and Denominator
questions.worked_solution:
We start by factoring the function as much as possible and canceling the common factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+2x-3}{2{x}^{2}-x-1} & =\frac{(x-1)(x+3)}{(2x+1)(x-1)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{(x-1)}(x+3)}{(2x+1)\cancel{(x-1)}} \\  & =\frac{x+3}{2x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

We now set the denominator equal to zero:

$$
2x+1=0\,⟹\,x=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

So the *only* vertical asymptote is at $x=-\frac{1}{2}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying When a Rational Function has no Vertical Asymptotes
questions.worked_solution:
Let's simplify the expression by factoring both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4{x}^{2}-3x}{8x-6} & =\frac{x(4x-3)}{2(4x-3)}=\frac{x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the denominator is never zero, we conclude that this function has no vertical asymptotes. A plot of the function is below. Note that it is not defined at $x=\frac{3}{4}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Vertical Asymptotes for the Sum of Two Rational Functions
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's put the two terms over a common denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{x+3}-\frac{1}{x-6} & =\frac{x-6-(x+3)}{(x+3)(x-6)}=-\frac{9}{(x+3)(x-6)}\end{aligned}
$$

There are no common factors in the numerator and denominator, so we proceed to set the denominator equal to zero and get

$$
(x+3)(x-6)=0\,⟹\,x=-3\,,\,x=6.
$$

Therefore, the vertical asymptotes are at $x=-3$ and $x=6.$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Vertical Asymptotes for the Sum of Two Rational Functions
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's put the two terms over a common denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{x-1}+\frac{1}{x+1} & =\frac{x+1+(x-1)}{(x-1)(x+1)}=\frac{2x}{(x-1)(x+1)}\end{aligned}
$$

There are no common factors in the numerator and denominator, so we proceed to set the denominator equal to zero and get

$$
(x-1)(x+1)=0\,⟹\,x=1\,,\,x=-1.
$$

Therefore, the vertical asymptotes are at $x=1$ and $x=-1.$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining Vertical Asymptotes of Rational Functions by Factoring the Numerator and Denominator
questions.worked_solution:
We start by factoring the function as much as possible and canceling the common factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4x-12}{3{x}^{2}-9x} & =\frac{4(x-3)}{3x(x-3)} \\  & =\frac{4\cancel{(x-3)}}{3x\cancel{(x-3)}} \\  & =\frac{4}{3x}\end{aligned}
$$

We now set the denominator equal to zero:

$$
3x=0\,⟹\,x=0
$$

So the *only* vertical asymptote is at $x=0.$
